title: The Hierophant

seo.title: Destiny matrix 5 — The Hierophant: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: The Hierophant is arcanum 5 in the destiny matrix: the energy of knowledge and of passing it on, in its strong and weak version.

meaning: The fifth arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of meaning and of passing it on. Its point is simple: take something complicated — another person’s experience, a law, a method — and put it across so that people understand it and can use it. If a 5 stands in your chart, you carry the role of The Hierophant: the one others come to for an explanation and for footing, a translator between the murky and the plain.

What moves this number is the need to understand. Until the meaning is found, a five has no peace; the moment it has worked something out, it wants to hand that understanding on. The energy is steady and unhurried: it does not race ahead and does not invent from nothing, but looks for a tested footing — a school, a tradition, a teacher — and builds its own on top of it.

The main conflict of a five is between its own voice and someone else’s authority. It is easy for a five to stand behind a tradition and speak in its words, and just as easy to mistake being right for the truth. A living five keeps meaning open: it doubts, it checks, it leaves room for other people’s experience. A frozen one turns into a broadcaster defending the form long after the content has left it.

Being this arcanum means running almost everything through the question “what is the sense of this”. In the strong version that is a gift: the complicated becomes short and clear, and the people who need such footing gather around on their own. In the weak version the same confidence hardens into the pose of the eternal elder, and no one is left to talk with: the person is right, but alone.

A five is easy to tell from its neighbours by the task it takes on. The four, The Emperor, builds structure and keeps order by the strength of form; a five fills that same form with meaning and explains what it is for. The six, The Lovers, leads through feeling and the choice of two; a five joins people another way — through shared understanding and knowledge passed on. Its place is the bridge, not the throne and not the union.

article.title: 5 in the destiny matrix — The Hierophant, the arcanum of teachers, tradition and a promise kept
article.short: In the destiny matrix, 5 is The Hierophant, also known as the Priest and the Teacher. The fifth arcanum governs knowledge that is not kept to oneself but handed on: from teacher to pupil, from elders to the young, from a tradition to those who join it. All of its themes gather around this one idea — study and mentoring, belonging to “your own people” (a school, a family, a profession) and the word you give: a contract, a vow, a marriage. In the plus, a 5 is the kind of person you talk to and walk away with everything clear. In the minus, it is the one who lectures uninvited and defends a rule that lost its meaning long ago. It is one of the most common arcana in the matrix: 83.4% of people have a 5 somewhere in their reading, so what matters is not the number itself but the point where it stands.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 5: The Hierophant — meaning in the plus and minus
seo.description: Destiny matrix 5 is The Hierophant: teacher, tradition and the word you give. Where a 5 stands, program 5, its three tails, love, money and compatibility.

ul: **Names:** The Hierophant, the Priest, the Teacher; in old decks, the Pope.
**Essence:** knowledge that has become common property — a teaching, a tradition, a rule, a rite.
**In the plus:** explains hard things clearly, studies seriously, keeps their word, gathers their own people around them.
**In the minus:** lectures uninvited, hides behind authority, lives “the proper way”, keeps the truth back “for your own good”.

**Without a calculator:** born on the 5th or the 23rd — your personality portrait is a 5; born in May — your spiritual task; born in 1949, 1958, 1967, 1976, 1985, 1994, 2003, 2012 or 2021 — your material task.

sections.h2: The one who shows what is sacred
paragraphs: The word “hierophant” is Greek, and it means, quite literally, “the one who shows the sacred” (hierós, sacred; phaínein, to show). At Eleusis it was the title of the high priest of the Mysteries — the man who, on the great night of the rite, revealed the holy objects to the initiates. He had not made them, and they were not his. His work was to show them, so that people could see.

That is the whole of the 5. It is the arcanum not of the one who knows, but of the one through whom knowledge reaches others. The High Priestess (2) keeps knowledge within, The Emperor (4) builds order, and The Hierophant makes knowledge shared: explains it, teaches it, turns experience into a method, a rule, a rite, a school. Without him, knowledge stays in one head and leaves with it.

So the 5 always stands in between. Between teacher and pupil — and over a lifetime it usually plays both parts. Between the older and the younger. Between “the way we do things here” and the person who has just walked in. By nature a 5 is rarely a loner: it needs people to learn from and people to pass things on to. While the chain runs in both directions, the energy is in the plus. Where it jams at one end, the arcanum’s familiar minuses begin.

One caveat straight away: a 5 does not oblige you to teach at a school, and it does not make you religious. You can teach driving, page layout, baking or negotiation. A tradition can be a family recipe, a professional standard or the house rules of your team. The fifth arcanum is about how knowledge passes from hand to hand, wherever that happens.

sections.h2: Three themes of the 5: knowledge, belonging, the given word

paragraphs.h3: Knowledge: learn it, understand it, pass it on

paragraphs: A strong 5 studies seriously: with a master, within a school, by a method, not from scraps. Knowing is not enough — it needs to understand how a thing works. And then it can explain it to someone else. It is easy to spot. A colleague has been wrestling with a report for three days; you spend ten minutes showing how it is put together, and a week later they do it on their own. That is the fifth arcanum: not doing the job for someone, but making sure they understand it.
The shadow of this theme is getting stuck at one end of the chain: only hoarding knowledge “until I’m ready”, or only handing it out without asking whether anyone wants it.

The 5 is also the sense of belonging. People like this hold together the holiday dinner where everything is just as Grandma used to make it, the class reunion, the work chat where somebody explains to the newcomer how things are done around here. They know the norms and, more importantly, understand what the norms are for. Around such a person others have somewhere to come in: a family, a profession, a circle.

The flip side is living for the approval of your own. “What will people say?” becomes the main question, and your own opinion goes into hiding so that you do not fall out of the circle. The tarot author Benebell Wen hears “a dark undertone” in this card: the pressure to conform and the stigma that falls on those who choose to live differently. The snobbery of “the initiated” grows from the same root: we know the right way, the rest do not.

paragraphs.h3: The given word: contract, vow, marriage

paragraphs: The third theme is the given word. A 5 keeps promises, values agreements and likes a relationship to be named and made official. Among the divinatory meanings Waite gives the card, four words stand in a row: “Marriage, alliance, captivity, servitude”. They read easily as one thing in two states. A vow that a person chose and keeps on choosing is an alliance. A vow held up only by “that’s how it’s done” is captivity.
The same goes for any rule. A living rule remembers why it was made. A dead one answers the question “why?” with a single word: “tradition”.

sections.h2: The 5 in the plus and in the minus
paragraphs: The plus and the minus of the 5 are not two different people but one and the same quality in two different states.

head: In the plus
In the minus
rows: Explains hard things so that someone else can put them to use
Explains when nobody asked; a conversation turns into a lesson

Studies instead of doing: “not ready yet” for years on end
Relies on tested experience
Offers a quotation instead of an opinion: “my teacher said so”, “it is written”
Keeps their word and their agreements
Keeps a rule that lost its meaning long ago
Guards the traditions of the family and the trade
Says “we don’t do that here” instead of explaining
Gathers their own people — a school, a team, a family
Splits people into insiders and outsiders, the initiated and the rest
Merciful and patient with those who are learning
Patient only with those who agree
Tells the truth with care

paragraphs: Describing this card, Waite added a warning that explains nearly every minus of the 5 at once. The pontiff, he writes, may forget “the significance of this his symbolic state” and act “as if he contained within his proper measures all that his sign signifies or his symbol seeks to shew forth”. The teacher starts to speak as though they were the truth itself, the keeper of a tradition as though they were the tradition, the parent as though they were the rule. From that moment knowledge stops passing through the person and gets stuck in them: they no longer show, they own. And arguing with them becomes almost impossible, because you are no longer arguing with them but with “all the right-thinking people” in whose name they speak.

Wen adds one more familiar story: the truth kept back with the best of intentions. “Better he doesn’t know.” “Let’s not upset the children.” Such protection, she writes, “will hurt the Seeker more than it helps”: nobody has the right to decide for another person what they should know, because “we are not the keeper of others”. For a 5 this is an especially treacherous trap, because from the inside it looks like care.

sections.h2: How to tell whether you have a 5
paragraphs: Three points of the chart come straight from your date of birth:

ul: **personality portrait, point A**, also called the calling card — the day: a 5 for everyone born on the 5th or the 23rd (2 + 3 = 5);
**spiritual task, point B** — the month: a 5 for everyone born in May;
**material task, point C** — the sum of the digits of the year: a 5 for 1949, 1958, 1967, 1976, 1985, 1994, 2003, 2012 and 2021.

paragraphs: The other points are built by adding these three together, and the calculator gets them faster. There a 5 turns up even more often, and the reason is arithmetic. When a sum is greater than 22, its digits are added up, and three different sums become 5: 23, 32 and 41. So in the points built by addition the 5 is one of the most frequent arcana, and in the karmic task and the point under the heart it is the most frequent of all.

paragraphs.h3: If you have more than one 5

paragraphs: Almost half of all people have a 5 in two or more places in the chart. That does not mean they have “twice as much” Hierophant: each 5 plays its own part. Someone born on 23 May 1985 has a 5 in the personality portrait, the spiritual task and the material task at once — and these are three different questions: how people see them, what draws them from within, and how they build their work. Read each one on its own, then look at how they add up.

In two points a 5 never falls, whatever the date of birth: the entry of relationships and the tail (the point on the lower ray closest to the centre) and the spiritual purpose. That is how the formulas work: only multiples of three appear there — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. If you have come across a reading of “5 in the spiritual purpose”, it was calculated by a different scheme or got wrong.

In classical numerology 5 is the number of freedom, change and movement — almost the opposite of The Hierophant. In the destiny matrix the figure 5 is the number of a tarot card, and it means what the fifth arcanum means.

sections.h2: The 5 in every point of the chart
paragraphs: The same energy answers different questions in different points. The table shows where a 5 can appear, what share of people have it there (counted over every date of birth from 1900 to 2026) and what it says in that place. Topics with a detailed reading of their own are given as links.

paragraphs: A 5 also turns up in the reading by decades — for 48% of people. The age scale runs along the outer points of the chart: the personality portrait governs the first ten years of life, the spiritual task the years from 20 to 30, the material task from 40 to 50, the karmic task from 60 to 70, and the family points the stretches in between. Such a decade most often passes under the sign of apprenticeship, your own or someone else’s: the person looks for a mentor, truly masters a trade or takes on pupils for the first time.

sections.h2: The karmic tail and the program of the 5
paragraphs: The karmic tail is the three lower numbers of the chart, running down from the centre: the entry, the middle and the karmic task. In the destiny matrix it is read as a storyline a person has brought with them and easily repeats until they notice it. One person in five has a 5 in the tail — 21.1% — and there are only three variants. A 5 never appears at the entry of the tail, so here it is either the middle or the root.

When the 5 is at the root, in the place of the karmic task, it is the lesson itself: to build your own relationship with rules and authority. When it is in the middle, the 5 is the mechanism, the thing that keeps the old circle turning: a rule, a rank or a vow that long ago became a chain.

ul: **[15-20-5](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-20-5)** — the most common of all 26 possible tails, found in 10.1% of people. The 5 is at the root. Popular readings call it the “Rebel”: a pull stronger than any rule (The Devil, 15) and an instant protest at someone else’s “that’s not how it’s done” (Judgement, 20). The task of the 5 here is neither to wage war on other people’s rules nor to give in to them, but to find a rule you would sign up to yourself.

**[15-5-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-5-8)** — 9.2% of people. The 5 is in the middle, between The Devil and Justice (8). Popular readings call it “Betrayal in the Family”: an oath or a family law turns into shackles over time, and then comes judgement, someone else’s or your own.

**[6-5-17](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-5-17)** — 1.8% of people. The 5 is in the middle, between The Lovers (6) and The Star (17). Popular readings call it “Pride”: a person starts living by other people’s ratings, and every talent becomes a rung on a ladder of rank. The task is to give your light without waiting for applause.

paragraphs: In two tails out of three the 5 sits next to The Devil, and for a reading that is a very telling neighbour. The Hierophant is a bond a person accepts of their own free will: a teaching, a vow, a rule. The Devil is a bond that holds them against their will: craving, fear, dependence. Tails with this pair show how one quietly turns into the other — and how to turn it back.

paragraphs.h3: The program of the 5: what goes round in circles

paragraphs: When people search for “program 5”, they usually mean a 5 in the points that make up a program — the karmic task or the centre of the chart (how programs work is explained [on a separate page](/programs)). A program is a storyline that repeats itself, with different people and in different settings. The 5 has four such storylines, and each one is recognised by its ending.

**The uninvited teacher.** You see how it ought to be done, and you explain. Nobody listens. You step back with a bitter “I told you so” — and next time you explain even harder. At a family dinner your brother hears not advice about his business but yet another lecture, and next time he simply won’t tell you what is going on. The way out is to answer the question you were asked, not the one you think they should have asked.

**The eternal student.** One more course, one more book, one more mentor — while your own business, your own consulting, your own writing keep being put off because “it’s too early”. Whatever the question, the person answers in someone else’s words. The way out is to release one thing into the world, imperfect as it may be, and sign it with your own name.

**The proper way.** Life runs by someone else’s rulebook: a profession the parents approved of, a marriage because “it’s time”, rules nobody ever checked. The person tries hard to do everything right and waits for it to be noticed and appreciated — and it isn’t. The way out is to test every rule with the question “why?” and keep the ones that have a living answer.

**The kindly secret.** The truth is held back to protect someone — and it surfaces at the worst possible moment, along with resentment at the silence. The way out is to tell the truth carefully and in measured doses, but to tell it.
Neither the tail nor the program is a sentence or a debt you have to “work off”. It is a habitual move that kicks in before you have time to choose. Notice it, and the choice is already there.

The 5 is the arcanum of a union sealed by a word, and it brings seriousness to a relationship. It matters to a 5 that the couple share values and have things to talk about: the union rests not on household routine alone but on a shared sense of how to live and what for. A 5 likes a relationship to be named and made official, and a family to have its own holidays and its own way of life.

The difficulties grow out of that same seriousness. One partner gradually takes the mentor’s chair, and every argument becomes an exam the other has failed in advance. Other people’s rulebooks move into the home: “in my family we did it this way”, “Mum thinks otherwise”. For more on how the arcanum sounds in a couple, see [5 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/5) and [5 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/5).

At work a 5 is strongest where something complicated has to be made clear, or where rules and standards come first: mentoring and teaching, staff training and course design, law, editing and translation, guided tours and popular science, archives, museums and libraries, service in a religious community, certification and quality control, sports refereeing. In any profession a 5 sooner or later becomes the one who shows newcomers the ropes. And it usually earns not from a product but from what it knows and can explain.

The typical trap is endless preparation: “once I finish one more course, I’ll start charging”. The knowledge piles up, while people who know just as much get paid because they dared to go out to people sooner. More in [5 on the money line](/encyclopedia/position/money/5) (the question about a “5 under the dollar sign” belongs there too: that is what people call a 5 in the middle of the money line, point R2) and in [the talent of the 5](/encyclopedia/position/profession/5).

sections.h2: The 5 for women and for men
paragraphs: Gender plays no part in the calculation: the matrix adds up only the day, month and year of birth, and a man and a woman born on the same day have exactly the same numbers. The meaning of the arcanum does not change with gender either.

What changes is something else: which ready-made rules the people around you offer. And ready-made rules are The Hierophant’s very subject. So the questions “how a woman ought to behave” and “what a real man should be” are not background for a 5 but its direct work: to accept these rules as your own, to rewrite them or to turn them down — but consciously, not because that is how your parents did it.

A woman with a strong 5 may keep the family’s way of life, or she may found a school of her own — and the second is every bit as much a 5 as the first. A man with a 5 may become a mentor, a man of faith, the elder of his family — or an interpreter of complex ideas for thousands of people. The arcanum sets the theme, passing on knowledge and your stance towards rules, not a role you have to play.
Here it is important to tell two cases apart.

**A 5 in the partners’ personal charts.** If one or both of them have it, values and rules — “the way we do things” — are a strong theme in the couple. Common ground comes quickly when their views coincide, and hard when each has brought their own rulebook into the home. Two fives under one roof would do well to agree in advance which things one of them teaches and which the other.

**A 5 in the couple’s matrix.** This matrix is calculated separately: the matching points of the two personal charts are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22. The calculation is set out step by step in Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book “Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost” (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility), and there the couple’s points mean something different from the points of a personal chart. A 5 in the couple’s matrix describes a union of the traditional kind: the couple have their own rules and stick to them; the partners are friends as well, with shared views and plenty to talk about; authority in the family is accepted willingly, and money is handled carefully and jointly. The flip side is the urge to remake each other, lecturing, intolerance of other opinions, and relatives who get too far into the couple’s life. The author’s advice to such couples is to get on with the relatives but not to let them inside their boundaries, and to start holidays and traditions of their own rather than only inheriting other people’s.
The matrix gives no compatibility percentage. A 5 in a couple is not a score for the union but a description of what holds it together and what it may trip over.

A year under the 5 is a time to lean on what others have already tested: to go and study, to find a mentor, to put agreements in writing. What it brings and where it gets stuck is covered in [arcanum 5 for the year](/year/5).
The 5 is easier to understand once you set it beside the cards it resembles.

ul: **The High Priestess (2).** Both cards are about knowledge, but The High Priestess knows silently and from within, while The Hierophant teaches out loud. Waite draws the line in exactly this way: he is “the ruling power of external religion, as the High Priestess is the prevailing genius of the esoteric, withdrawn power”. [The High Priestess and The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/2-5).

**The Emperor (4).** Both stand for power, but of different kinds. The Emperor rules what can be built and defended, The Hierophant what people believe in and consider right. Wen puts it like this: “If The Emperor is about having authority from government or the Father, then The Hierophant is about having authority from the Divine.” [The Emperor and The Hierophant](/encyclopedia/combination/4-5).

**The Lovers (6).** The Hierophant joins people by rule and vow, The Lovers by feeling and choice. A union needs both; in the 6-5-17 tail these cards stand side by side. [The Hierophant and The Lovers](/encyclopedia/combination/5-6).

**The Hermit (9).** Also a teacher, but a different one. The Hierophant teaches many — to a syllabus, in a school, within a tradition. The Hermit seeks along his own path and shares what he finds with whoever comes to him of their own accord. [The Hierophant and The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/5-9).
**The Devil (15).** The shadow of the 5: a bond that holds you against your will. [The Hierophant and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/5-15).

sections.h2: Waite’s Hierophant: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: In the Waite–Smith deck (1909) The Hierophant wears a triple crown and sits between two pillars. Waite points out at once that “they are not those of the Temple which is guarded by the High Priestess”: hers is the way into the hidden, his is the open, outer side of the teaching. In his left hand The Hierophant holds “a sceptre terminating in the triple cross”. His right hand is raised in “the well-known ecclesiastical sign which is called that of esotericism, distinguishing between the manifest and concealed part of doctrine”. And Waite adds: “It is noticeable in this connexion that the High Priestess makes no sign.”

At The Hierophant’s feet lie crossed keys, and two ministers kneel before him; Benebell Wen notes that one is “cloaked in red roses and another in white lilies”. The keys stand for “the power of the keys”: in Christian tradition the keys promised to the apostle Peter mean the right to “bind and loose” — to decide what is allowed and what is not. Waite approves of the formula given by Grand Orient, who “says truly that the Hierophant is the power of the keys, exoteric orthodox doctrine, and the outer side of the life which leads to the doctrine”. The amusing part is that Grand Orient, whom Waite praises for accuracy, is Waite himself: it is the pen name under which he had earlier published a book on fortune-telling with cards.

Then comes the heart of it. Waite’s Hierophant is “the summa totius theologiæ, when it has passed into the utmost rigidity of expression”, and at the same time he symbolises “all things that are righteous and sacred on the manifest side”. He is “the channel of grace belonging to the world of institution as distinct from that of Nature”; he is “the order and the head of the recognized hierarchy, which is the reflection of another and greater hierarchic order”. He is not philosophy, he is not inspiration, and he is not religion itself, “although he is a mode of its expression”. Hence the warning about the pontiff who forgets that he is only a sign.

Lay The Devil (15) from the same deck beside him and you will see a rhyme: again a figure raised up high and two people below, only instead of ministers there are chained captives. A vow and a chain are built alike; the difference is whether a person is held by choice or by fear.

paragraphs.h3: The fifth arcanum in a tarot reading

paragraphs: In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings the upright Hierophant is “Marriage, alliance, captivity, servitude; by another account, mercy and goodness; inspiration; the man to whom the Querent has recourse”. Reversed: “Society, good understanding, concord, over-kindness, weakness.” Benebell Wen reads the card in a modern key: upright, “conforming to what is the present norm, membership in the majority, and having the approval of those in power”; reversed, nonconformity, your own path in defiance of the rules — and for her that is, if anything, a good sign: “The Hierophant in reverse is considered a good omen card.”

In the destiny matrix a card is never reversed: the calculated number simply stands in its point. The plus and the minus of the 5 are two ways of living one and the same energy, not the position of a card in a spread.

sections.h2: Pope, Priest, Teacher: why the card has so many names
paragraphs: In the Italian decks of the Renaissance and in the French Tarot de Marseille the fifth arcanum is simply the Pope. Waite lists other names too — the High Priest, the Spiritual Father, even the Abbot — and remarks: “I think, however, that in its primitive form this card did not represent the Roman Pontiff.” In the eighteenth century, in the so-called Besançon tarot, the Pope and the Popess were replaced altogether by Jupiter and Juno: the seat of highest authority remained, and only the figure on it changed.

It was the Frenchman Antoine Court de Gébelin who tied the fifth arcanum to hierophants, in 1781: he believed the tarot was a legacy of Egyptian priests and looked for traces of the ancient mysteries in its cards. More than a century later, in the English Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, to which Waite belonged, the hierophant was the officer who led the initiation rite, and the Waite–Smith deck fixed the name. It is more precise than “Pope”: the point is not a particular church but anyone who brings a person into a circle of knowledge. The word “pontiff” has a lovely inner form as well: Latin pontifex is built from the words for “bridge” and “to make”. Historians still argue about where the title really came from, but the image of a bridge suits the fifth arcanum perfectly.

In Russian-language destiny matrix readings the names that took hold are the Priest and the Teacher. The Teacher is the most practical of them: it tells you straight away what this energy is busy with in life.

sections.h2: How to live the 5 in the plus

ol: **Ask before you teach.** “Do you want advice, or do you just want me here?” — one question like that, and the conversation stops being a lesson.
**Keep the chain alive at both ends.** Find someone to learn from right now — a living person, not only books. And someone to teach: pass one of your skills on to one person.
**Test rules with “why?”.** If the only answer to why something is done is “that’s the custom”, the rule has to be either filled with meaning or let go.
**Speak in the first person.** Instead of “it is generally held” and “according to so-and-so’s method” — “I think” and “I have checked”.
**Welcome disagreement.** A good teacher is glad of a pupil who goes further. The best test is whether people can argue with you and stay on good terms.

**Review your vows.** Once a year, ask yourself about your main commitments: would I choose this again? If yes, it is a union. If I hold on only because “I have to”, it is time for an honest conversation.
**Don’t keep the truth back “for their own good”.** Before you stay silent, ask yourself: in their place, would I want to know?
**Start a tradition of your own.** Don’t only inherit a way of life — create one: a small ritual, a holiday, a rule that keeps your people together.

paragraphs: A good hierophant is known not by how much they know but by how many people around them have learned to understand things for themselves.
